done.why: I got lost in a maze of Oddly-angled Rooms south of the Menhir Room. I never found the stone door with the question.

about: An exploration of a Zork-like underground empire, reached through a barrow. A Wizard says the treasures are south of the ravine: pearls behind a stone door that asks a question, and more past a room that won't keep still. The place seems to want you to collect those treasures.

moments.note: The Wizard gave a clear hint about where the treasure is and what guards it.
The yellow sphere was an illusion the Wizard's word conjured, and the room said so wryly.
The Carousel floor was turning under me, and the exits change on every attempt.
Passing through the curtain of light and the wall led between the bank rooms in ways I could not map.
The Oddly-angled Rooms are an unmappable maze where the descriptions are nearly identical.
The Dragon Room is dangerous but gave me no clear way to deal with the dragon.

wished: A way to tell the maze rooms apart
Some way to find the stone door with the question
A way to stop the carousel

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: It gave me a concrete goal.

lines.line: It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.

fun.why: The early hints and prose were good, but I spent the later turns in a confusing maze.

engagement.why: The stated goal kept me moving until I hit the maze.

difficulty.why: Disorienting rooms and the maze blocked me, and I never found the stone door.

interestingness.why: It is a rich Zork-like map, with the wizard's illusions and the bank's strange mechanics.

prose.why: The wry, witty lines stood out against the classic room text.
